text:
ajay: Quick design q — how should the serving layer signal a phased variant drain to routers/orchestration? want minimal blast radius and smooth fallback. :thinking:

samira: i'd prefer an explicit state machine: ACTIVE -> DRAINING -> DRAINED. DRAINING denies new session leases but lets existing sessions finish within TTL.

maria: also need a contract for fallbacks: when a variant is DRAINED, routers should route to fallback variants defined by traffic weights + hard fallback order. fallback order must be deterministic.

kevin: +1. another requirement: metrics AND a readiness probe tie. if error rate spike or latency regression, switch variant to DRAINING automatically and start fallback.

ajay: sounds good. edge cases: what if a long-lived session prevents progress? we can't block rollout forever. maybe a max-drain window after which we evict?

samira: yeah add two timers: soft TTL for polite drain, hard cutoff for eviction. hard cutoff should trigger an eviction event and increment a rollback metric. ops can configure.

kevin: we should also support per-customer pinning: some customers can be opted into variant for longer, do not evict their sessions early. add customer-level exemptions in the lease policy.

maria: will need schema for these rules. draft config idea: 
```yaml
variant_policy:
  id: v2026-03-01
  on_health_fail: DRAINING
  drain_ttl_seconds: 600  # soft
  hard_cutoff_seconds: 3600
  fallback_order: [v2026-02-15, vstable]
  customer_pin_exemptions: [cust-42, cust-314]
```

ops_bot: deploy-check: policy-schema v1/ok (lint passed) :white_check_mark:

ajay: love the draft. question: who owns the decision to mark DRAINING? the runtime, the canary controller, or automated signal from telemetry?

samira: layered approach: controller initiates DRAINING for planned rollouts; telemetry/alerting can auto-toggle to DRAINING if thresholds tripped; runtime can request DRAINING if local health is bad. all should go through a single arbitration service to avoid conflicting commands.

kevin: arbitration service must produce a single source-of-truth state with provenance fields (actor, cause, timestamp). routers read that SOT and apply rules.

maria: concerning session affinity — routers should evaluate affinity on a per-session basis: if session started before DRAINING, keep it on variant until TTL/hard cutoff. new sessions get routed per fallback order.

ajay: what about partial responses or batching tasks in-flight? need to ensure the runtime drains kv-caches and completes background batches. add a graceful shutdown hook in runtime that returns last-seen-kv and flushes pending batches.

kevin: suggest adding a small API for runtime -> orchestrator: POST /_drain?variant=v2026-03-01 returns {accepted: true, soft_ttl: 600, hard_cutoff: 3600}. orchestrator then emits 'DRAINING' SOT.

maria: also track a numeric 'drain_score' so we can prioritize evictions: old sessions with low activity get evicted first. boolean eviction alone is rough.

ajay: good call. last big thing: rollback circuit — if fallback variant also fails or capacity exhausted, orchestrator should attempt multi-step fallbacks and eventually signal throttling or route to degraded-mode (smaller model/response). keep SLOs transparent.

samira: make sure the console shows live drain status per variant, active session count, pinned-customer list, and predicted time-to-drain. operators will want a one-click abort to cancel DRAINING.

dev-bot: FYI pushed RFC stub to /docs/rfcs/phased-drain-contract.md (WIP). please review.

kevin: next actions: ajay to update API prototype, maria to sketch policy schema, samira to draft arbitration state machine, i'll mock console UX. sync tomorrow 10am. :+1:
